events.description: President Biden speech announcing full US withdrawal from Afghanistan by 11 Sep 2021 (20th anniversary of 9/11)
US–Taliban withdrawal agreement signed in Doha; required Afghan government (not a party) to release 5,000 prisoners; Section 1F bars US military action against Afghanistan
US raid kills Osama bin Laden in Abbottabad, launched from Afghanistan
Jalaluddin Haqqani helped Osama bin Laden escape Tora Bora
Farouq al-Qahtani, al-Qaeda commander in eastern Afghanistan, killed by US
US cruise missile strikes on bin Laden camps after embassy bombings ('cruise missiles and empty tents')
TTP attacks on Pakistan Army GHQ Rawalpindi, Lahore, Islamabad; controlled large areas of northwestern Pakistan
Resolute Support stopped releasing district-level Taliban control data
Bill Roggio published 'The War in Afghanistan is over. We had lost.'
Taliban demand release of additional 7,000 prisoners and sanctions delisting if US stays past May 1
CIA Director Burns says CT options will be constrained and visibility lost after withdrawal
New York Times publishes op-ed in Sirajuddin Haqqani's name, called disinformation by hosts

key_claims: There is no genuine peace process; staying longer to negotiate a Taliban–Kabul settlement was never a viable option.
The Haqqani Network was integrated with the Taliban from the early 1990s; Jalaluddin Haqqani incubated the first generation of al-Qaeda and helped bin Laden escape Tora Bora in 2001.
Sirajuddin Haqqani, Taliban deputy emir, is 'in bed with' al-Qaeda per bin Laden files and US designations, yet receives no scrutiny while Ghani does.
Al-Qaeda's oath of loyalty runs from affiliates (e.g. Shabaab) to Zawahiri and through him to Taliban emir Hibatullah Akhundzada.
Insurgencies are the lifeblood of international terrorism; al-Qaeda figures like Farouq al-Qahtani did both insurgency and external ops from Afghanistan.
AQ leaders elsewhere (Batarfi/AQAP, Abu Humam al-Shami/Hurras al-Din) are Afghan jihad veterans who fought for the Taliban before 9/11.
TTP's charter was written with al-Qaeda help; a resurgent Taliban/AQ will embolden a renewed TTP push against nuclear-armed Pakistan.
The Taliban has not fulfilled any counterterrorism assurance of the Doha deal; Section 1F is a 'poison pill' barring future US action in Afghanistan.
Choosing 11 Sep 2021 as the withdrawal date hands the Taliban and al-Qaeda a propaganda victory; the next AQ generation will claim to have defeated America.
